raw: Tap Activate on the app under Cards → New card and follow the on-screen instructions. The app never asks you to type the full card number or PIN to activate. The new card works straight away from the online portal.

Cash deposited at a Chinor ATM is credited immediately, and cash deposited at a branch counter is credited by the end of the same business day. Chinor does not accept cheques, so a cheque cannot be credited. If a cash deposit is still missing after that time, a human agent can check it with the deposit receipt.

A transfer shows Scheduled until it leaves Chinor and Sent afterwards. Domestic transfers to other banks arrive the same business day if sent before 16:30, otherwise the next business day; international transfers take 2–4 business days. While it is Scheduled you can still cancel it in the app.

A reverted card payment is usually a pre-authorisation — for example at a hotel, fuel pump or car rental — that the merchant did not settle, so the reserved amount was released back to your balance. Pre-authorisations are released automatically after 9 business days at the latest.

Identity verification is required by anti-money-laundering law before an account can be used; it also protects your account from being opened or used by someone else. It takes a passport or national ID card and a selfie video, and is usually completed within 2 hours.

First check that the card is activated and not frozen, and that the relevant toggle under Cards → Security (contactless, online or ATM) is switched on. Then cancel the payment and try it again; if it fails both ways, a human agent can review the transaction.

A card top-up is normally instant but can take up to 2 business days when the card issuer holds it; an amount is then reserved in the app until it is confirmed. If the time has passed, ask your card issuer why the payment was declined.

PIN and full card number are never asked for; if a human agent asks for them, raise the issue in in-app chat.

A replacement is free on Standard and 35,000 UZS on Plus; the fee is waived on both plans for the first replacement each calendar year. If the new card fails, the app shows the problem and asks you to try again.
